raw_case_text:
A 64-year-old man with no comorbidities presented with painful nodular lesions on his left foot following a traumatic injury. On examination, there were enlarging nodules that progressed to purulent lesions with sanguinolent discharge, draining fistulas, and elimination of grains. A clinical diagnosis of mycetoma was made and a biopsy was performed. The histopathological evaluation revealed granulomas and fibrosis. It was also remarkable for the presence of grains and filamentous structures compatible with an actinomycetoma (Figure 1-A, B,C). Multiple tissue cultures were negative, and the causative agent was presumed to be Nocardia spp. based on clinical and histopathological findings.
The patient was treated with trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (TMP-SMX) for eight years, without complete resolution of symptoms, as he had persistent painful nodular draining lesions (Figure 2-A). A new culture was obtained from the draining secretion, and Gordonia soli was recovered by culture and identified using 16S rRNA gene sequencing. He was treated with three courses of a 3-week regimen of intravenous linezolid (600 mg every 12 h) plus meropenem (1 g every 8 h) administered at intervals of 24 weeks, and oral TMP-SMX (8 mg/kg/day of the TMP component) was maintained between and after the courses. He experienced significant improvement in pain, edema, and resolution of the purulent discharge.
Following adequate symptom resolution, maintenance therapy with TMP-SMX was discontinued. Four years later, the patient experienced pain recurrence, edema, purulent discharge, and elimination of grains through the fistulas (Figure 2-B). A new specimen was obtained from the secretion, and the grains were observed using direct microscopy (Figure 1-D). The causative organism was cultured (Figure 1-E) and the genus Gordonia identified by MALDI-TOF MS (score 1.62) (Bruker MALDI Biotyper), which was confirmed as Gordonia soli by 16S rRNA gene sequencing, indicating persistence of infection. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the foot revealed signs suggestive of inflammation in the subcutaneous tissue; midtarsal and tarsometatarsal joints; and the calcaneum, midfoot, and metatarsal bones, suggesting osteomyelitis. The "dot-in-circle" sign was present, which is suggestive of mycetoma (Figure 2-C). The patient was treated with another two courses of intravenous linezolid plus meropenem, with significant improvement in symptoms, and maintenance therapy was indicated with oral TMP-SMX plus ciprofloxacin (500 mg every 8 h).

subjective.chief_complaint: A 64-year-old man presented with painful, enlarging nodular lesions on his left foot with purulent-sanguinolent discharge, draining fistulas, and grain elimination following prior foot trauma.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Following a traumatic injury to the left foot, the patient developed painful enlarging nodules that progressed to purulent lesions with sanguinolent discharge, draining fistulas, and elimination of grains. After an initial presumptive clinical/histopathological diagnosis of actinomycetoma treated with oral trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (TMP-SMX) for 8 years without complete resolution, and subsequent courses of intravenous linezolid plus meropenem, he experienced recurrence 4 years after stopping maintenance TMP-SMX with pain, edema, purulent discharge, and grain elimination through fistulas.
subjective.past_medical_history: History of prior traumatic injury to the left foot; no other medical comorbidities.

objective.physical_examination: Enlarging painful nodules on the left foot with edema, purulent and sanguinolent discharge, draining fistulas, and elimination of visible grains.
objective.routine_investigations: Direct microscopy of draining secretions demonstrated characteristic grains; initial multiple tissue cultures were negative.
objective.advanced_workup: Initial skin biopsy histopathology revealed granulomas, fibrosis, grains, and filamentous structures compatible with actinomycetoma. At late relapse, foot MRI demonstrated subcutaneous tissue inflammation, involvement of the midtarsal and tarsometatarsal joints, osteomyelitis of the calcaneum, midfoot, and metatarsal bones, and the pathognomonic 'dot-in-circle' sign of mycetoma.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Actinomycetoma complicated by pedal osteomyelitis caused by Gordonia soli (initially misattributed to Nocardia spp. on histopathology alone) was definitively confirmed when cultures of draining secretions grew Gordonia soli, identified via MALDI-TOF MS (Bruker MALDI Biotyper score 1.62) and confirmed by 16S rRNA gene sequencing both after 8 years of failed TMP-SMX monotherapy and again upon relapse 4 years later. Treatment with three 3-week courses of intravenous linezolid (600 mg q12h) plus meropenem (1 g q8h) at 24-week intervals with inter-course oral TMP-SMX (8 mg/kg/day of TMP) initially resolved symptoms; following late relapse 4 years after stopping maintenance therapy, two additional courses of intravenous linezolid plus meropenem followed by maintenance oral TMP-SMX plus ciprofloxacin (500 mg q8h) achieved significant clinical improvement.
